key_insight: In entropy variables, the nonlinear Entropy Stable Extension becomes a fourth-order quasi-cubic system whose quasi-linear approximation preserves entropy stability and the highest-order derivative terms.
engineering_relevance: The closure offers a continuum-model route to improved rarefied-gas heat-transfer predictions beyond Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations.
method: Reformulate the closure using an identity for the derivative of the inverse linearized collision operator.
Apply an entropy-stable quasi-linear approximation to stationary heat transfer between parallel plates.
Analyze plane-wave dispersion in the one-dimensional linearized equations.
evidence_signal: For the tested heat-transfer setting, interpolating boundary conditions yield temperature profiles closer to DSMC and heat flux closer to Sherman–Lees than Navier–Stokes–Fourier predictions; all frequency modes in the linearized dispersion analysis are stable.
watch_item: The heat-transfer improvement depends on boundary-condition specification, while the reported dispersion stability concerns one-dimensional linearized equations.
paper_title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
